failureModes.prompt: Before it is switched off, should people get a stated period to download everything they made?
failureModes.why: after the switch-off, anything people did not download is lost permanently, and they need a date to plan around

options.label: A stated period, such as 30 days
options.consequence: people can move their work, and the switch-off date is fixed in advance

options.label: Switch off on the announced day
options.consequence: quicker, and people lose whatever they had not saved elsewhere

failureModes.recommended: A stated period, such as 30 days
failureModes.provenBy: a dated notice sent to every active account, and a test that a full download works for an account until the last day

failureModes.prompt: When charges stop at switch-off, should customers be refunded for time they already paid for?
failureModes.why: subscriptions keep renewing until cancelled in the billing system or app store, and people who paid in advance lose that money without a refund

options.label: Refund unused time
options.consequence: costs some revenue, and nobody pays for something that no longer exists

options.label: No refunds, charges stop only
options.consequence: keeps revenue, and people who paid in advance lose money

failureModes.provenBy: a billing report after switch-off showing no active renewals, and a refund recorded for each customer with unused paid time

failureModes.prompt: Should outside developers and connected services get a dated notice before their access stops?
failureModes.why: systems built by others stop working when an interface they call disappears, and nobody can prepare for a change that was never announced

options.label: A dated notice, with warnings in responses
options.consequence: a little work now, and connected systems have time to change

options.label: Switch off without notice
options.consequence: nothing to do now, and other people's systems stop working on the day

failureModes.recommended: A dated notice, with warnings in responses
failureModes.provenBy: a recorded notice sent to every API key holder, and a test that responses carry a Sunset header with the switch-off date

failureModes.prompt: After switch-off, should every server, key and outside account be closed from a written list?
failureModes.why: a forgotten key still works for whoever holds it, and idle servers and accounts keep charging until someone closes them

options.label: Close everything from a written list
options.consequence: a day of careful work, and nothing keeps charging or stays open to misuse

options.label: Switch off the main servers only
options.consequence: quicker, and forgotten keys and accounts keep costing money or get misused

failureModes.recommended: Close everything from a written list
failureModes.provenBy: the written list with each server, key and outside account marked closed or revoked, and a check that the old keys are refused

failureModes.prompt: After switch-off, should the domain stay registered, showing a notice to anyone who follows an old link?
failureModes.why: old links and email addresses still lead to the domain, and anyone who buys a lapsed domain receives that traffic and mail

options.label: Keep the domain, show a closure notice
options.consequence: a small yearly fee, and nobody else can receive mail sent to old addresses

options.label: Let the domain lapse
options.consequence: no further cost, and anyone can buy it and receive mail meant for us

failureModes.recommended: Keep the domain, show a closure notice
failureModes.provenBy: a check that the domain renewal is paid for a stated number of years, that old links show the closure notice, and that store listings are removed

failureModes.prompt: After switch-off, when should the data people left behind be deleted?
failureModes.why: the DPDP Act of 2023 in India and the GDPR in the EU require a business to erase personal data once its purpose has ended

options.label: On a stated date after switch-off
options.consequence: people know the deadline, and nothing is kept longer than promised

options.label: Keep it with no end date
options.consequence: nothing to schedule, and old personal data remains a breach and legal risk

failureModes.recommended: On a stated date after switch-off
failureModes.provenBy: a scheduled deletion job with the stated date, and a check after that date that no personal records or backups remain
